name: Aegean Loft Suite
terrace: 18 m² private terrace with day bed
blurb: A single lime-washed room under a cedar ceiling, with the whole western sea in the doorway.
lede: The smallest of our residences and the one guests ask for again. One room, one terrace, and nothing between the bed and the horizon but a pair of cedar shutters.
description: The Aegean Loft sits at the top of the west terrace, where the path runs out and the view opens. The room is one volume: a vaulted ceiling in cedar, walls finished by hand in lime, a stone floor that stays cool through August. Furniture is spare and low, so nothing competes with what is outside the door.

The terrace is the other half of the suite. A canvas day bed under an olive, a table for two, and an outdoor shower screened in dry stone. Most guests take breakfast there, then again at sunset with something from the bar.

name: Olive Garden Suite
blurb: A walled garden of its own, under trees that were here long before the resort was.
lede: Cooler than the sea-facing rooms and quieter than all of them. The garden suites open onto their own walled patch of the old grove.
description: Six olive trees on this plot are more than two hundred years old, and the wing was set out around them rather than through them. The result is a suite whose terrace is a room in its own right: dry stone walls at shoulder height, gravel underfoot, shade from morning until the light goes amber.

Inside, the room faces east, so it wakes gently and stays cool in the afternoon. It is the residence we suggest to guests who sleep lightly, and to anyone spending the middle of the day reading rather than swimming.

name: Cycladic Terrace Suite
blurb: A deep vaulted room that opens along its whole length onto a terrace set for dinner.
lede: The classic Elysis room: a barrel-vaulted ceiling, three arched doors onto the terrace, and a table where most guests end up eating at least once.
description: This is the plan the architect drew first and the one the rest of the resort grew from. The vault runs the length of the room and the three arched doors fold back completely, so in the evening the terrace and the room become the same space.

The terrace looks across the bay to the headland, which means sun from mid-morning and the last of the light at the far end of the day. In-suite dining is served here, and the kitchen will lay a table for six if you ask.

name: Salt White Suite
blurb: The quietest room in the house, off a courtyard with a fig tree and a single lantern.
lede: Set back from the sea and priced accordingly, without giving up anything that matters: the same beds, the same marble, the same breakfast.
description: The Salt White rooms sit around a small courtyard on the landward side, where the walls hold the cool and the only sound after eleven is the wind in the fig. They are the rooms our own team book when family visits.
Everything inside is identical to the sea-facing suites. What you trade is the horizon, and what you get back is silence and a rate that lets you stay a week instead of three nights.

name: Meltemi Junior Suite
bed: One king and a day bed
blurb: A sitting room as well as a bedroom, and the terrace that catches the north wind in August.
lede: Named for the wind that makes a Cycladic August bearable, and sited to take it. A separate sitting area makes this the smallest residence that works for three.
description: The Meltemi is a junior suite in the true sense: the bed sits in its own alcove behind a half wall, with a proper sitting area in front of it and a day bed that a third guest sleeps on comfortably.
Its corner of the terrace is the coolest place on the property in high summer. There is a reason the loungers here are booked out first in the first week of August.
amenities: Day bed for a third guest

highlights.v: Three, or a longer stay for two

name: Thalassa Pool Suite
terrace: 34 m² terrace with 4 x 3 m plunge pool
blurb: A heated plunge pool on a walled terrace, four steps above the sea path.
lede: The first of the pool suites, and the one closest to the water. The pool is heated from April and screened on three sides, so it is yours from breakfast until well after dark.
description: Thalassa takes the lower terrace, where the ground drops towards the sea path and the walls can be kept low without losing privacy. The pool is four metres by three, heated in the shoulder months, and lit from below at night.
Inside, the room is arranged around the view rather than the bed: a long window seat under the west window, and the bed set back where it stays dark in the morning.

name: Kyma Pool Suite
terrace: 38 m² terrace with 5 x 3 m pool
blurb: The westernmost residence, with a pool that finishes level with the horizon.
lede: Built on the point, where the terrace wall is the last thing between you and open water. The pool is cut to catch the sun until the moment it goes.
description: Kyma stands alone on the western point, which gives it two things nothing else here has: no neighbour on either side, and a straight, uninterrupted sunset from the water. The pool edge is set flush with the terrace so that swimming in it, the sea and the pool read as one surface.
The room behind is deliberately simple. A vaulted ceiling, a wall of cedar joinery, and a bed you can see the sea from without sitting up.
amenities: Heated 5 x 3 m pool with flush edge

name: Helios Pool Villa
bed: One king and a day bed
terrace: 60 m² terrace with 8 x 3 m pool
blurb: A one bedroom villa on its own path, with an eight metre pool and a kitchen you can actually cook in.
lede: The first of the freestanding villas. Its own gate, its own path down to the sea, and a pool long enough to swim lengths in before breakfast.
description: Helios is a whole small house: entrance courtyard, living room, separate bedroom, two bathrooms, and a galley kitchen fitted properly rather than token. Guests who stay a fortnight tend to take this one and cook once or twice a week.

The terrace runs the length of the building and steps down twice, so the pool, the dining table and the loungers each sit at their own level. The lowest step is the one to be on at seven in the evening.

highlights.v: Two or three, staying a while

name: Selene Pool Villa
bed: One king and a day bed
terrace: 64 m² terrace with 8 x 3 m pool
blurb: Helios's twin on the cool side of the hill, with a moon terrace and an outdoor bath.
lede: The same plan as Helios, turned to face north west. It loses an hour of afternoon sun and gains the coolest evening terrace at Elysis.
description: Selene was built as the pair to Helios and set on the opposite slope. The change of aspect matters more than the plan: the terrace here is shaded by two o'clock and cool by five, which in July is worth more than another hour of sun.
A copper bath stands on the upper terrace under a reed canopy, filled on request with hot water and sea salt. It is the detail guests write to us about afterwards.

name: Oleander Villa
bed: One king, two singles, one day bed
terrace: 80 m² terrace with 10 x 4 m pool
blurb: Two bedrooms either side of a living room, a ten metre pool, and oleander over every wall.
lede: The first of the two bedroom villas, laid out so that the two ends of the house are genuinely separate. Families and pairs of couples take this one.
description: The plan puts a bedroom at each end with the living room, kitchen and terrace between them, which is the difference between a villa that sleeps four and one that four people can actually live in. The second bedroom takes two singles or a second king.
The pool is ten metres and unheated by choice; by late May it holds the day's heat until midnight. The garden around it is the oldest planting on the property.

name: Myrtos Villa
terrace: 72 m² terrace with 9 x 4 m pool
blurb: Set high in the grove, with two equal bedrooms and the best shade on the property.
lede: Two matched king bedrooms, which is what two couples travelling together actually want, and a terrace under old trees rather than under canvas.
description: Myrtos sits at the top of the grove where the trees are thickest. Both bedrooms are the same size and have the same bathroom, so nobody is quietly given the worse room.

The terrace is shaded by the grove itself for most of the day, which keeps the house ten degrees cooler than the sea-facing villas in August and makes long lunches at the outdoor table possible at any hour.
amenities: Outdoor dining for eight under the trees

name: Anemos Residence
bed: Two kings and a day bed
terrace: 95 m² terrace with 12 x 4 m pool
blurb: A twelve metre pool on the headland, a proper kitchen, and a cook who will use it.
lede: The first of the residences: a house with staff attached. Breakfast is cooked in your own kitchen, and dinner can be too.
description: Anemos takes the whole west headland. The living room opens on two sides, the pool runs twelve metres along the seaward edge, and the kitchen is a working one, with a six burner range and a cold room rather than a token hob.
A residence booking includes a cook for breakfast each morning and the option of a chef for dinner, arranged the day before. Guests who take Anemos for a week usually eat in three or four nights.
amenities: 12 x 4 m heated pool on the headland

highlights.v: A family, or a week of hosting

name: Kastro Residence
bed: Three kings, one convertible to twins
terrace: 120 m² terrace with 14 x 4 m pool
blurb: Built around the shell of a nineteenth century watchtower, with three bedrooms and the longest pool at Elysis.
lede: The oldest structure on the estate and the largest of the three bedroom residences. The tower is now the library; everything else was built around it.
description: The watchtower on this corner was a ruin when the land was bought, and the condition of keeping it was written into the plans. Its ground floor is now a small library with the original stone left exposed, and the residence wraps around it in two low wings.
Three bedrooms, each with its own bathroom, a living room that seats ten, and a fourteen metre pool along the terrace edge. At night the lights of Naoussa are visible across the water from the pool.
amenities: Chef and server for dinner on request
Private gate and parking for two cars

highlights.v: Three couples, or a family of six

name: Elaia Family Residence
bed: One king, two twin rooms, one cot
terrace: 100 m² terrace with 12 x 5 m pool, shallow end
blurb: Designed around children: a shallow pool end, a walled lawn, and bedrooms that are actually near each other.
lede: The residence we built after a decade of watching families try to make a luxury villa work with a four year old in it.
description: Everything here answers a practical problem. The pool has a shallow shelf at the near end and a gate on the terrace. The two twin rooms sit either side of the main bedroom rather than across the house. There is a lawn, which on a Cycladic hillside takes some doing, and it is walled.
The kitchen is stocked before you arrive from a list you send us, and Little Elysis, the kids club, is a three minute walk down the path.
amenities: 12 x 5 m pool with shallow shelf and gate
Cot, high chair and buggy on request

name: Lighthouse Loft
terrace: 70 m² over two levels, roof terrace
position: The point, above the beach path
blurb: A split level on the point with a roof terrace, sea on three sides and a stair down to the beach path.
lede: Two floors on the narrowest part of the point. Sea through every window, a roof terrace above the roofline of everything else, and thirty steps to the water.
description: The lower floor holds the two bedrooms, cut into the rock and cool all day. Above them the living room opens on three sides, and above that the roof terrace looks over the whole bay with nothing in the way.
Sunrise and sunset are both visible from the roof, which is true of no other residence here. Breakfast is served up there if you want it, and the bar will set up for eight.
amenities: Direct stair to the beach path

highlights.v: Two couples who want the view

name: Aithra Penthouse
terrace: 140 m² roof terrace with 10 x 4 m pool
position: Above the main house, private lift
blurb: The whole top of the main house: a rooftop pool, an outdoor kitchen and a private lift.
lede: A hundred and forty square metres of roof terrace with a ten metre pool on it, reached by a lift that stops nowhere else.
description: Aithra occupies the entire upper floor of the main house. The interior is two bedroom suites and a living room; the point of it is what is outside, where the terrace runs the full footprint of the building with a pool along the western edge and an outdoor kitchen at the other end.
The bar sends someone up at seven each evening unless you tell them not to. It is the residence taken for anniversaries and, twice a season, for a proposal.
amenities: Evening bar service on the terrace

name: Elysis Beach House
terrace: 110 m² deck with 10 x 4 m pool, on the sand
position: South end of the private beach
blurb: The only building on the sand: a two bedroom house with a deck, a pool and the bay for a garden.
lede: At the far end of the private beach, where the rock closes the bay. Step off the deck onto sand, and there is nobody between you and the water.
description: The Beach House was the original fisherman's store and is the only structure at sea level. It was rebuilt in timber and stone with a deck across the whole front, a pool set into it, and two bedroom suites behind.

Its own stretch of beach is screened by the rock at the south end, so it stays private even when the beach club is busy. The bonfire on Thursday nights is lit fifty metres from the deck, which guests either love or ask us to move; it does not move.
amenities: Kayaks and paddleboards at the door

highlights.v: The only residence at sea level
At the edge of the deck
Swimmers, and the fire on Thursdays

name: Nefeli Estate
view: The whole bay, from the ridge
bed: Four kings, two convertible to twins
terrace: 220 m² terraces with 18 x 5 m pool
blurb: Four bedrooms on the ridge with an eighteen metre pool, a staffed kitchen and a gate of its own.
lede: The whole ridge, taken as one house. Four bedroom suites, an eighteen metre pool, and a team of three who work only for the estate while you are in it.
description: Nefeli is the largest thing Elysis has and the least visible: it sits behind the ridge line, screened from the rest of the resort by the grove, with its own gate off the coast road and a drive that goes nowhere else.

Four bedroom suites open onto a courtyard; the living rooms and the long terrace face the bay. A cook, a housekeeper and a house manager are assigned to the estate for the duration of a booking, and the wine cellar downstairs is stocked to a list you send ahead.
amenities: Private wine cellar, stocked to order
Gated drive and parking for four cars

highlights.v: A family taking the whole ridge
